chunks: When you intend to depart, say: Peace be upon you, the peace of one who departs, neither weary nor speaking (of parting) nor lingering, and the mercy and blessings of Allah.

O People of the House of Prophethood, 'Indeed, He is Praiseworthy, Glorious' [Quran 15:87]. Peace be upon you as the peace of a guardian who is not desirous of leaving you, nor replacing you, nor preferring others over you, nor deviating from you, nor neglecting your nearness.
May Allah not make this the final visitation of your graves and the coming to your shrines.
And peace be upon you, and may Allah gather me in your company, and grant me to drink from your basin, and make me part of your faction.
And may you be pleased with me, and turn me over in your dominion, and give me life in your return, and make me ruler in your days.
And may He accept my effort through you, and forgive my sin through your intercession, and pardon my stumble through my love for you, and raise my status through my allegiance to you.
And honor me through your obedience, and grant me dignity through your guidance, and make me among those who return successful, victorious, gaining, safe, healthy, wealthy, and triumphant.
By the pleasure of Allah, His bounty, and His sufficiency, with the best that any of your visitors, allies, lovers, and followers returns with.
And grant me the return, then the return, forever, as long as my Lord keeps me alive.
With sincere intention, faith, piety, humility, and abundant, pure, permissible sustenance.
O Allah, do not make this the final visitation of them, remembrance of them, and prayer upon them.
And decree for me forgiveness, goodness, mercy, blessing, piety, success, light, faith, and the beauty of acceptance.
As You have decreed for Your allies who know their right, those who necessitate their obedience, who desire their visitation, and who draw near to You and to them.
My father, mother, soul, family, and wealth are sacrificed for you.
Make me in your concern, and place me in your faction, and include me in your intercession, and remember me before your Lord.
O Allah, send prayer upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and convey to their souls and bodies from me peace. And peace be upon him and upon them, and the mercy and blessings of Allah.

key_terms.أَهْلَ بَيْتِ اَلنُّبُوَّةِ: People of the House of Prophethood

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication recited when leaving the shrines of the Imams in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this Ziyarat al-Wadāʿ serves as a comprehensive farewell prayer to the Ahl al-Bayt, emphasizing the spiritual bond of *walayah* and the hope for continued visits. It uniquely petitions for inclusion in their *hizb* (faction) and requests that the current visit not be the final one, reflecting the Shia eschatological expectation of the Imam's return. The supplication integrates themes of intercession (*shafa'ah*) and divine favor, anchoring the visitor's status within the broader cosmic hierarchy of the Prophet's household.
